findings.claim: REQ-01-004 says every route in this spec answers a client contact 404; TC-01-INT-01 asserts the settings pair answers that same client contact 403. No implementation satisfies both, and the reason the contracts give for the 403 does not hold for a client principal.

witness.detail: REQ-01-004: 'IF a client contact requests any route in this spec, THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL answer 404.' TC-01-INT-01: 'Sign in as a client contact of an organization and call all four routes' → 'GET /api/organizations/{orgId}/portal/settings → 403 TEMPLATE_MESSAGES.generic.forbidden'; the same split is in contracts §Routes and in README §Shared Rules. The contracts justify it with 'CapabilityGuard has already proven the caller is a member of this organization' — but OrgScopeGuard (apps/api/src/auth/org-scope.guard.ts:44-50) throws a bare NotFoundException for `request.principal?.kind === 'client'` on every /api/organizations/:orgId route whose handler or class does not carry @AllowClientPrincipal(), and it runs before CapabilityGuard in every controller's @UseGuards list. So one implementation registers the settings routes like every other organization route and answers the contact 404, satisfying REQ-01-004 and failing TC-01-INT-01; the other adds @AllowClientPrincipal() to the settings pair so CapabilityGuard is reached and answers 403, satisfying TC-01-INT-01, failing REQ-01-004, and contradicting contracts §Security's 'A client principal reaches nothing here.'

findings.suggestedFix: One sentence deciding it: either REQ-01-004 gains an exception naming the settings pair and contracts §Security is amended to say a contact reaches the guard there, or TC-01-INT-01's settings assertion becomes 404 and the README's Shared Rule is narrowed to 'a member of this organization who lacks the capability'.

findings.claim: REQ-01-018 falls back to Organization.countryCode for a member who states no country, and the README presents that chain as the one time-off already owns. PATCH-012 removed that fallback from the product and the code holds no such chain, so the portal would answer a different country than every other screen for the same member.

witness.detail: specs/portal/README.md §Related Areas: 'specs/time-off/ — owns the country-resolution chain the holidays block uses: a country stated on the membership, falling back to Organization.countryCode. REQ-01-018 states that chain in full rather than pointing at it.' specs/patches/PATCH-012-a-member-states-their-own-country-or-none.md §The rule: 'THE SYSTEM SHALL resolve a member's holiday country from the country stated on their own membership, and from nothing else' and 'THE SYSTEM SHALL pay a member with no resolved country the global holidays only — the rows carrying no country — in the Holidays summary, in the time-off calendar, in the holiday list read as mine, and in Amounts Owed.' The code agrees with the patch: packages/validation/src/reports.ts:566-573 (`resolveMemberHolidayCountry` reads only `membershipCountry` and returns null when it is blank) and apps/api/src/holidays/holidays.service.ts:111-118 ('PATCH-012 — the caller's own stated country. A caller who states none sees the global rows only, rather than the ones the organization's country would have lent them'). Scenario: an organization with countryCode 'US' and a member whose membership states none, with one US holiday and one global holiday seeded. GET .../holidays?scope=mine answers the global holiday alone; GET .../portal/home under REQ-01-018 answers both, and TC-01-INT-07 asserts it must.

findings.suggestedFix: Either drop the third link — REQ-01-018 resolves the membership's country and nothing else, REQ-01-019 becomes 'a member who states no country', TC-01-INT-07's second leg changes — or state deliberately, in this spec's own text, that the portal reinstates the organization fallback that PATCH-012 removed and why one screen may answer a different country than the calendar and the payroll report do. The README's Related Areas sentence is false either way and must go.

findings.claim: `client-added` is a first-class entry kind that is derived, group-switched, role-filtered, asserted by an integration case and given a page — and no requirement says what that page carries, no document states the sentence the feed draws for it, and no mock state draws one.

witness.detail: REQ-01-032 derives a `client-added` entry from every Client at createdAt; REQ-01-034's table marks it Drawn for admin and manager; REQ-01-036 puts it in the Work group; TC-01-INT-10 asserts 'admin and manager are answered four entries' and 'user and viewer are answered three — the same set minus the client-added entry'; REQ-01-038 says every entry the caller's feed would contain has a page answering 'the facts its kind carries'. The facts-per-kind requirements are REQ-01-042 (vacancy-opened), REQ-01-045 (member-joined, member-anniversary) and REQ-01-046/047 (project-started). There is no requirement for client-added. Contracts §Routes shows `facts` 'ordered by the server, so the page never decides what to draw first', which makes its contents a server decision the spec must make. Separately, the sentence: 01-home.mock.html's nine states contain member-joined ('Anna Petrova joined the team as a Frontend Engineer.'), vacancy-opened ('A vacancy is open: Senior React Developer.'), project-started ('Aurora started for Northwind Ltd.') and member-anniversary ('Ivan Demchenko has been with the team for 2 years.') and no client-added entry at all, and the contracts' GET .../portal/news example body carries none either. Concretely: an admin seeds a client named 'Northwind Ltd' and opens `client-added:{clientId}`. One implementation answers facts [Added, by whom] with the sentence 'Northwind Ltd was added as a client.'; another answers facts [Projects, Contacts] with 'A new client: Northwind Ltd.' Both satisfy every sentence in the bundle, TC-01-INT-10 passes under both, and no case distinguishes them — which means the copy and the page are decided by whoever implements them first.

findings.suggestedFix: One requirement beside REQ-01-042/045/046 saying what a `client-added` entry page answers, and the entry's sentence written down where the other four are — either a mock state or a line in `## Screens`. If the kind is not meant to have a page, say so in Out of Scope and state what REQ-01-038 does with its id.
